definition_en: ordinary and happening every day; not special
core_image: 每天背的那只旧书包：普通却可靠
scene: 巷口早餐铺每天清晨升起同样的白汽。 Carrying an old school bag is part of his everyday routine.
sceneCN: 这里 everyday 是「日常的」（第 1 个义项：普通且每天发生）；句意是背旧书包是他日常习惯的一部分。

derivatives.zh: 拆开的短语形式，义为「每天」，作时间状语
较罕见派生词，义为「日常性；平淡」
相关词，义为「例行公事」，常与 everyday 搭配

senses.title: Ordinary and daily
senses.definition: happening or used every day, ordinary and not special
senses.definitionCN: 每天发生或使用，普通而不特别
senses.example: She wore her everyday clothes to the market.
senses.exampleCN: 她穿着便服去市场。
senses.why: Every plus day fuses into one adjective: the day that happens again and again.
senses.whyCN: every 与 day 融合成一个形容词：日复一日的那一天。

senses.title: Commonplace, not remarkable
senses.definition: very ordinary, without anything special about it
senses.definitionCN: 十分普通，毫无特别之处
senses.example: The magician turned everyday objects into surprises.
senses.exampleCN: 魔术师把寻常物品变成惊喜。
senses.why: Repetition dulls wonder, so the word also means unremarkable.
senses.whyCN: 重复使惊奇变钝，于是词义也指平凡无奇。

intro.en: Everyday is the closed-up form of the phrase every day. When the phrase became an adjective, the space closed and the stress moved to the first part.
intro.cn: everyday 是短语 every day 的合写形式。短语转为形容词后，空格闭合，重音移到前部。

items.en: Every was already fused from ever and each in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: every 在十三世纪已由 ever 与 each 融合而成。

items.en: The phrase every day appeared in Middle English as a plain time expression.
items.cn: 短语 every day 在中古英语中作为朴素时间表达出现。

items.en: Writers began closing the phrase to everyday when using it before nouns as an adjective.
items.cn: 作家在名词前作形容词使用时开始将短语合写为 everyday。

items.en: Dictionaries recorded the closed form in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 词典在十八世纪收录合写形式。

items.en: Modern style guides now teach the split: everyday clothes but I read every day.
items.cn: 现代文体指南区分：everyday clothes 与 I read every day。

note.en: The first group collects the everyday family; the second collects near meanings about ordinariness.
note.cn: 第一组收集 everyday 词族的成员；第二组收集与「平凡」相关的近义词。

entries.definition: two words, an adverbial of time meaning each day
entries.definitionCN: 每天（两词短语）。作时间状语，不是形容词。

entries.definition: the quality of being ordinary
entries.definitionCN: 日常性；平淡。由 everyday 加 -ness 构成。

entries.definition: a day on which one works, or the hours of a working day
entries.definitionCN: 工作日；工作时长。复合词，结构相似。

entries.definition: normal, not different or special
entries.definitionCN: 普通的。强调与他人无异。

entries.definition: happening once a day, often about routines
entries.definitionCN: 每日的。侧重频率一天一次。

entries.definition: seen everywhere, therefore dull
entries.definitionCN: 平凡的；司空见惯的。书面语，略带贬义。

normalIntro.en: Five concrete hooks built from the spelling rule and real contrasts.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于拼写规则与真实对比的具体联想。

normal.en: Closed everyday is the adjective; open every day means each day.
normal.cn: 合写 everyday 是形容词；分开 every day 是「每天」状语。

normal.en: Everyday life is the most common phrase of the family.
normal.cn: everyday life 日常生活，最常用搭配。

normal.en: Compare: I read every day, and it is my everyday habit.
normal.cn: 对比句：I read every day（分开），my everyday habit（合写）。

normal.en: Everyday clothes are the opposite of Sunday best.
normal.cn: everyday clothes 便服，与 Sunday best 盛装相对。

normal.en: The sound hints at loving every ordinary day, for spelling only.
normal.cn: 谐音：「爱夫瑞的每一天」——每天都平常地爱着，帮助拼读，不是词源。

abstract.en: Picture the same old school bag by the door each morning.
abstract.cn: 画面：每天清晨门边同一只旧书包。

abstract.en: Feel the morning bus arriving at exactly the usual minute.
abstract.cn: 感觉：晨间公交准点到达的平常一刻。

abstract.en: Smell the same breakfast steam rising from the same stall.
abstract.cn: 嗅觉：巷口早餐铺升起同样的白汽。

examples.en: Riding the bus is part of my everyday life.
examples.cn: 坐公交车是我日常生活的一部分。

examples.en: These everyday objects can all become science tools.
examples.cn: 这些日常物品都能变成科学工具。

examples.en: He practices everyday English with his pen pal.
examples.cn: 他和笔友练习日常英语。

sensesIntro.en: Everyday covers both the daily and the ordinary: what happens every day becomes what is nothing special.
sensesIntro.cn: everyday 兼指「每天发生的」与「平常的」：日复一日之事即寻常之事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same worn school bag by the door each morning.
core.cn: 核心意象：每天清晨门边同一只旧书包。

intro.cn: everyday 是合写复合词，构成部分都是朴素的日耳曼语词。

I walk to school every day.

items.example: Birthday and everyday share the day ending.

definition_en: the amount of space between two places or things
core_image: 两点之间那段量得出来的空
scene: 操场尽头立着旗杆，体育老师用步子一段段量过去。 The school is within walking distance of the station.
sceneCN: 这里 distance 是「距离、一段路」（第 1 个义项：两地之间的空间量）；句意：学校离车站步行即到。

derivatives.zh: distance 的形容词形式，义为「遥远的」
distant 加副词后缀构成，义为「遥远地」

senses.title: Space between two places
senses.definition: the amount of space from one place to another
senses.definitionCN: 从一个地方到另一个地方的空间量
senses.example: The distance from home to school is two kilometers.
senses.exampleCN: 从家到学校的距离是两公里。
senses.why: The Latin root stare means to stand: distance is first the space that stands between two points.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 stare 意为「站立」：distance 最先指立在两点之间的那段空。

senses.title: A far-away point or view
senses.definition: a place or view that is far away
senses.definitionCN: 遥远的地方或景物
senses.example: We saw a tower in the distance.
senses.exampleCN: 我们看见远处有一座塔。
senses.why: The space between points becomes the far zone where things grow small and blurred.
senses.whyCN: 点与点之间的空，延伸成事物变小、变模糊的远区。

senses.title: Coldness between people
senses.definition: a feeling of not being close or friendly
senses.definitionCN: 不亲近、不友好的感觉
senses.example: There was a polite distance between the two teams.
senses.exampleCN: 两队之间保持着客气而疏远的关系。
senses.why: Physical gap is borrowed for the heart: people who stand far apart are not close.
senses.whyCN: 物理的间隔被借给内心：站得远的人自然不亲近。

intro.en: Distance comes from a Latin verb about standing: it is the space that stands between two things.
intro.cn: distance 来自一个关于「站立」的拉丁动词：它是立在两物之间的那段空。

items.en: Latin distantia comes from distare, to stand apart, from dis- apart and stare to stand.
items.cn: 拉丁语 distantia 来自 distare（分立而站），由 dis-（分开）加 stare（站立）构成。

items.en: Old French distance carried the same sense of space between points.
items.cn: 古法语 distance 保留了点与点之间空间的意思。

items.en: English borrowed distance in the fourteenth century for measured space.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语借入 distance，指可度量的空间。

items.en: The word widened to far-away views and to gaps in time.
items.cn: 词义扩大到远方景物与时间间隔。

items.en: Today distance also names emotional coldness between people.
items.cn: 如今 distance 也指人与人之间的情感疏远。

note.en: These words sit near distance in form or meaning.
note.cn: 这些词在形式或意义上与 distance 相邻。

abstract.en: Feel the cool air of a hilltop far from town.

abstract.en: See a boat shrinking to a dot on the horizon.
abstract.cn: 看小船缩成地平线上的一个点。

examples.en: The shop is a short distance from our gate.
examples.cn: 商店离我们大门不远。

examples.en: Lights twinkled in the distance after dark.
examples.cn: 天黑后远处灯光闪烁。

examples.en: Long-distance buses leave from that stop.
examples.cn: 长途汽车从那个站台出发。

definition_zh: 夫人；女士；太太；小姐；对女性的尊称；（俚语）鸨母
definition_en: a polite and respectful way of addressing a woman, or a woman who manages a brothel
core_image: 一位被恭恭敬敬称呼的女士：礼貌的称呼指向一位体面女性
scene: 酒店的经理亲自上前招呼那位提着行李的客人。 May I help you with your luggage, madam?
sceneCN: 这里 madam 是「女士、夫人」（第 1 个义项：对女性的礼貌尊称）；句意为经理恭敬地询问这位女客人是否需要帮忙提行李。图中可辨识物件：酒店大堂、行李箱、前台。

pos.zh: 名词：夫人、女士、太太、小姐；对女性的尊称；（俚语）鸨母

collocations.zh: 主席女士（对女主席的称呼）
先生或女士（不识对方时的称呼）

derivatives.zh: madam 的口语缩略形式，义为「夫人、女士」，多用于英式英语和服务场合

senses.title: A polite way to address a woman
senses.definition: a polite and respectful word used when speaking to a woman whose name you do not know
senses.definitionCN: 在不认识对方姓名时礼貌恭敬地称呼女性的用语
senses.example: May I take your coat, madam?
senses.exampleCN: 夫人，要我为您拿外套吗？
senses.why: The phrase originally meant my lady, so calling a woman madam places her in the honoured position of a lady.
senses.whyCN: 这个词原本的字面意思是「我的夫人」，所以称呼一位女性 madam，等于把她放到受尊敬的「贵妇」位置上。

senses.title: A formal address to a customer
senses.titleCN: 对女性顾客的正式称呼
senses.definition: a formal word used by shop assistants, waiters or hotel staff to address a female customer
senses.definitionCN: 店员、侍者或酒店工作人员称呼女性顾客的正式用语
senses.example: The waiter handed her the menu and said, "Madam, the soup of the day is mushroom."
senses.exampleCN: 侍者递上菜单说：「女士，今日例汤是蘑菇汤。」
senses.why: Service speech keeps the old courtly habit: the customer is treated as a lady of rank, so the honourable title survives.
senses.whyCN: 服务用语保留了旧日的宫廷礼节：顾客被当作有身份的贵妇来对待，因此这个尊称一直流传下来。

senses.title: A title in formal letters
senses.definition: a word used in the opening of a formal letter to a woman, as in Dear Madam
senses.definitionCN: 用于写给女性的正式信函开头，如 Dear Madam
senses.example: The letter began "Dear Sir or Madam" because the writer did not know who would read it.
senses.exampleCN: 信的开头是「尊敬的先生或女士」，因为写信人不知道谁会读到它。
senses.why: When the reader's name and sex are unknown, the polite title stands in for the name itself.
senses.whyCN: 当收信人的姓名和性别都不明确时，这个礼貌称呼就代替姓名来充当称呼。

senses.title: A woman of authority
senses.definition: a word used before an official title to address a woman holding that position, as in Madam Chairman or Madam President
senses.definitionCN: 用于官职前称呼担任该职位的女性，如 Madam Chairman、Madam President
senses.example: Madam Chairman, may I present the quarterly report to the board?
senses.exampleCN: 主席女士，我可以向董事会提交季度报告吗？
senses.why: A title of respect can be attached to any position of power, so the word marks the office, not just the person.
senses.whyCN: 尊称可以加在任何有权力的职位之前，因此这个词标记的是职位，而不只是某个人。

senses.title: A haughty or self-important woman
senses.definition: a humorous or critical word for a woman who behaves as if she deserves great respect and special treatment
senses.definitionCN: 戏谑或批评用语，指举止傲慢、自认为该受特殊待遇的女性
senses.example: She swept into the office like a little madam who owned the whole building.
senses.exampleCN: 她大摇大摆走进办公室，活像个把整栋楼都当成自己家的小姐。
senses.why: The honourable title can be used ironically: giving noble treatment to someone who merely acts noble is a common form of mockery.
senses.whyCN: 尊称可以被反用：对只是装出高贵样子的人刻意使用敬称，正是一种常见的讽刺手法。

senses.title: A brothel manager
senses.definition: in slang, the female manager of a brothel, often capitalized as Madam
senses.definitionCN: 俚语中指妓院的女经营者，常以大写 Madam 出现
senses.example: In the novel, the madam controlled every room in the house and every coin in the till.
senses.exampleCN: 小说里，这位鸨母掌管着屋里的每个房间和钱柜里的每一枚硬币。
senses.why: The manager runs the house the way a lady runs a great household, so the title of household authority was transferred to her trade.
senses.whyCN: 经营者像贵妇掌管大宅门一样掌管那栋房子，于是「家宅掌权者」的头衔被转移到了这个行当上。

intro.en: Madam is a shortened form of a French phrase meaning my lady, and its root is the Latin word for the mistress of a house.
intro.cn: madam 是法语短语「我的夫人」的缩略形式，其词根是拉丁语中「女主人」一词。

items.en: Latin domina meant mistress, lady of the house, the feminine of dominus lord. It later gave Dame and dame in many European languages.
items.cn: 拉丁语 domina 意为「女主人、夫人」，是 dominus「主人」的阴性形式；它后来在多种欧洲语言中产生 dame 一词。

items.en: Old French combined the possessive ma with dame into ma dame, a respectful way of addressing a lady of rank.
items.cn: 古法语把物主词 ma 与 dame 合成 ma dame，即「我的夫人」，是对有身份女性的敬称。

items.en: In speech the two words fused into a single form madame, which travelled to England with the French-speaking court.
items.cn: 在口语中两个词融合为单一名词 madame，并随讲法语的宫廷传入英格兰。

items.en: Middle English borrowed madame in the thirteenth century and soon clipped it to madam, and further to ma'am in casual speech.
items.cn: 中古英语在十三世纪借入 madame，很快截短为 madam，口语中又进一步缩略为 ma'am。

items.en: The polite senses stayed central, while the ironic use for a haughty woman and the slang use for a brothel manager grew out of the same title of authority.
items.cn: 礼貌义项始终是核心，而讽刺傲慢女性和俚语指鸨母的用法，都是从同一个「掌权者尊称」里长出来的。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the whole my-lady family in several languages; the near-meaning group gathers other polite ways of addressing a woman.
note.cn: 形近组收「我的夫人」这一词族在多种语言中的形式；近义组收其他称呼女性的礼貌用语。

normal.cn: madam 就是 ma dame（我的夫人）：两个法语词粘成了一个词。

normal.en: The root dame comes from Latin domina, the mistress of a house.
normal.cn: 词根 dame 来自拉丁语 domina，即一家之女主人。

normal.en: Letters that do not know the reader open with Dear Sir or Madam.
normal.cn: 不知道收信人的信件抬头写 Dear Sir or Madam。

normal.en: Shop staff and hotel clerks keep the word alive when serving women.
normal.cn: 店员和酒店职员接待女客时至今仍用这个词。

normal.en: In speech it shrinks to ma'am, one swallowed syllable.
normal.cn: 口语中它缩略成 ma'am，只剩一个吞掉的音节。

abstract.en: Picture a curtsy in a palace corridor: the word is that bow, folded small enough to carry in your mouth.
abstract.cn: 想象宫廷走廊里的一次屈膝礼：这个词就是那个礼，被折叠得刚好能放进嘴里。

abstract.en: Ma and dame sit side by side; whenever you own something politely in French, you put ma in front of it.
abstract.cn: ma 和 dame 并肩而立：法语里礼貌地「拥有」什么，就把 ma 放在前面。

abstract.en: One title, many women: the honoured lady, the haughty little madam, the woman who runs the house behind the door.
abstract.cn: 同一个称呼对应不同的女性：受尊敬的夫人、傲慢的大小姐、门后掌管全家事务的女主人。

examples.en: Madam, your table is ready; please follow me.
examples.cn: 女士，您的餐桌已备好，请跟我来。

examples.en: The application form began with the words Dear Sir or Madam.
examples.cn: 申请信的开头写着「尊敬的先生或女士」。

examples.en: She has grown into a little madam who refuses to carry her own school bag.
examples.cn: 她长成了个不肯自己背书包的大小姐。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「买的母」——买了单的是女主人，恭敬喊一声夫人；或记「骂得母」——再傲慢的夫人也不敢让人骂她母亲

root: 法语 madame 由 ma「我的」+ dame「夫人」构成；dame 源自拉丁语 domina「女主人」，阴性形式对应 dominus「主人」。从 ma dame「我的夫人」到 madame 再截短为 madam 与口语 ma'am。

sensesIntro.en: The senses of madam all radiate from one respectful title: serving a customer, opening a letter, honouring an office, mocking haughtiness, and naming a woman who commands a household of her own.
sensesIntro.cn: madam 的各个义项都从一个敬称向外辐射：服务顾客、开启信函、敬称官职、讽刺傲慢，以及称呼一位自己当家掌权的女性。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a respectful bow of words, my lady, offered to a woman who is treated as the mistress of the house.
core.cn: 核心意象：一次用词语完成的敬礼——「我的夫人」，献给被当作女主人对待的女性。

branches.en: THE POLITE LINE: unknown woman, served customer and unknown letter reader are all covered by the same respectful address.
branches.cn: 礼貌线：不识的女性、受服务的顾客、未知的收信人，都用同一个敬称来覆盖。

branches.en: THE OFFICE LINE: the title attaches to positions of power such as chairman or president.
branches.cn: 官职线：这个称呼可以加在主席、总统等有权力的职位之前。

branches.en: THE IRONIC LINE: honourable treatment given to someone who merely acts honourable becomes mockery.
branches.cn: 讽刺线：对只是装出高贵的人使用敬称，就变成了挖苦。

branches.en: THE HOUSEHOLD LINE: the mistress of a house becomes the manager of an establishment.
branches.cn: 家宅线：女主人变成了某个场所的经营管理者。

branches.en: THE FAMILY LINE: madame, mademoiselle, dame and ma'am are the same bow in other languages and shorter forms.
branches.cn: 词族线：madame、mademoiselle、dame 与 ma'am 是同一礼节在别的语言和更短形式里的样子。

intro.en: Madam is a phrase worn down to one word: a possessive and a noun of rank fused by daily speech.
intro.cn: madam 是被日常口语磨平的一个短语：一个物主词和一个表示身份的名词融合在一起。

latinIntro.en: Latin domina and dominus are fully recorded; the fused French forms madame and madam follow from ordinary sound change.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 domina 与 dominus 均有文献记录；法语融合形 madame 与 madam 是由普通语音变化自然产生的。

items.example: It is the masculine partner of the family root.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个词族的阳性对应形式。

items.example: It is the direct ancestor of dame.
items.exampleCN: 它是 dame 的直接祖先。

items.example: It stands before dame in the source phrase.
items.exampleCN: 它在源短语中位于 dame 之前。

items.example: It passed into English as dame and lady-rank words.
items.exampleCN: 它以 dame 等身份词的形式进入英语。

items.example: Speech merged ma and dame into one word.
items.exampleCN: 口语把 ma 与 dame 合并成了一个词。

items.example: English clipped the final vowel away.
items.exampleCN: 英语把词尾元音截掉了。

items.example: Fast speech swallows the middle syllable.
items.exampleCN: 快速语流把中间音节吞掉了。

items.example: The diminutive ending marks an unmarried woman.
items.exampleCN: 小称后缀标记未婚身份。

items.example: The same root governs the family of ruling words.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根还掌管着一族表示「统治」的词。

items.example: It keeps the sense of lordship.
items.exampleCN: 它保留了「主人身份」的含义。

derivatives.zh: madam 的口语缩略形式，义为「夫人、女士」
法语原形借词，义为「夫人、太太」
同一拉丁词根的古法语形式，义为「女士；女爵士」

definition_en: a person who has committed a crime; connected with crime or law-breaking
core_image: 被法律记下名字的人
scene: 模拟法庭活动里，扮演罪犯的同学低着头站上了被告席。 The criminal was caught near the park gate.
sceneCN: 这里 criminal 是「罪犯」（第 1 个义项：实施犯罪的人）；句意是那名罪犯在公园门口附近被抓获。

derivatives.zh: 基础名词，义为「犯罪；罪行」
由 crime 加 -ology 构成，义为「犯罪学」
由 criminal 加副词后缀构成，义为「犯罪地； criminally liable 依法负刑责的」

senses.title: A person who breaks the law
senses.definition: someone who has done something the law punishes
senses.definitionCN: 做了法律要惩罚之事的人
senses.example: Two criminals tried to hide in an old warehouse.
senses.exampleCN: 两名罪犯试图躲进一座旧仓库。
senses.why: The core image is a person carrying the charge named in court, so the doer inherits the crime's name.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是背负法庭罪名的那个人，所以行为者继承了罪行的名字。

senses.title: Connected with crime and punishment
senses.definition: relating to laws about punishable acts
senses.definitionCN: 与可惩罚行为的法律有关的
senses.example: Criminal cases are heard in a different court from family cases.
senses.exampleCN: 刑事案件在不同于家事案件的法庭审理。
senses.why: Once the word names the person, it also names the whole field of law around him.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既指人，也延伸指围绕他的整个法律领域。

senses.title: Shamefully wrong
senses.titleCN: 可耻的；极不应该的（比喻）
senses.definition: very wrong or unfair, though not against the law
senses.definitionCN: 非常错误或不公平，虽不违法
senses.example: It would be criminal to waste this once-in-a-lifetime chance.
senses.exampleCN: 浪费这次千载难逢的机会实在可惜。
senses.why: The court line again becomes a moral line, so unfair acts wear the same word.
senses.whyCN: 法庭的线再次变成道德的线，所以不公之事也穿上这个词。

intro.en: Criminal follows crime straight out of Latin judgement language.
intro.cn: criminal 顺着 crime 一路源自拉丁语的裁断用语。

items.en: The Latin crimen meant a charge or judgement point.
items.cn: 拉丁语 crimen 意为指控或裁断要点。

items.en: The adjective criminalis described matters brought before a court.
items.cn: 拉丁语形容词 criminalis 描述提交法庭的事项。

items.en: Old French carried criminel into its law vocabulary.
items.cn: 古法语将 criminel 带入法律词汇。

items.en: English borrowed criminel in the fourteenth century, at first as a law adjective.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入 criminel，起初是法律形容词。

items.en: The noun use for lawbreakers became the common everyday sense.
items.cn: 指违法者的名词用法成为日常常见义。

note.en: These words belong to the crime family or name law and guilt.
note.cn: 这些词属于 crime 词族，或指法律与罪责。

entries.definition: the illegal act itself
the study of crime
in a way punished by law
more than one criminal
one who breaks a rule or law
one who breaks the law
one who steals
one thought to be guilty
responsible for a wrong

normalIntro.en: Follow crime into its person form and its law form.
normalIntro.cn: 顺着 crime 看它的人形与法律形态。

normal.en: crime + inal = criminal, of crime or the person of crime.
normal.cn: crime + inal ＝ criminal，犯罪相关的或犯罪的人。

normal.en: Criminal law punishes; civil law settles debts.
normal.cn: 刑法惩罚，民法了结纠纷。

normal.en: A criminal record follows a person for years.
normal.cn: 犯罪记录会跟随人很多年。

normal.en: Catch the criminal: the police verb phrase.
normal.cn: catch the criminal：警方固定说法。

normal.en: Criminal waste means shamefully big waste.
normal.cn: criminal waste 指可耻的巨大浪费。

abstract.en: See handcuffs closing on a pair of hands at the park gate.
abstract.cn: 看公园门口一副手铐合拢在一双手上。

abstract.en: Hear the judge's list of charges being read out.
abstract.cn: 听法官逐条宣读罪名。

abstract.en: Feel anger at a broken promise to a whole team.
abstract.cn: 感受对一个团队失信的愤怒，那也是一种「罪」。

examples.en: The young criminal returned the stolen bike and said sorry.
examples.cn: 年轻的罪犯归还了偷来的自行车并道歉。

examples.en: Detectives studied the map for weeks to find the criminal.
examples.cn: 侦探们研究地图数周以找到罪犯。

examples.en: Throwing away school books is a criminal waste.
examples.cn: 扔掉课本是一种可耻的浪费。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克瑞米诺」——罪名「克」住他，「诺」言也救不了

root: 来自拉丁语 criminalis（提交法庭的），建立在 crimen（罪名）之上，经古法语 criminel 进入英语；既指「罪犯」，也指「刑事的」。

sensesIntro.en: From the person who crossed the line, to the law around it, to moral blame.
sensesIntro.cn: 从越线之人，到相关法律，再到道德指责。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a name written next to a charge
core.cn: 核心意象：写在罪名旁边的名字

branches.en: The person caught for the act
branches.cn: 因行为被抓的人

branches.en: Courts, records and police work
branches.cn: 法庭、记录与警务

branches.en: Shame without a courtroom
branches.cn: 无需法庭的可耻

branches.en: Person and law field together
branches.cn: 人与法律领域相连

branches.en: Waste and unfairness named criminal
branches.cn: 被称作 criminal 的浪费与不公

intro.en: Criminal wears a Latin adjective suffix on the crime root.
intro.cn: criminal 在 crime 词根上戴着拉丁形容词后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root crimen means charge or judgement.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 crimen 意为指控、裁断。

definition_en: a box that slides in and out of a piece of furniture
core_image: 带小拉手的滑动木盒
scene: 找橡皮找了半天，他终于拉开书桌最下面那层。 The ruler is in the top drawer of the desk.
sceneCN: 这里 drawer 是「抽屉」（第 1 个义项：家具中可推拉的盒子）；句意：尺子在书桌最上面的抽屉里。

derivatives.zh: drawer 构成的短语名词，义为「多屉柜」
drawer 的基础词，义为「拉；画」

senses.title: A sliding box in furniture
senses.definition: a box that slides in and out for storing things
senses.definitionCN: 存放物品、可推拉的盒子
senses.example: She keeps her erasers in the top drawer.
senses.exampleCN: 她把橡皮放在最上面的抽屉里。
senses.why: The box is named by its action: it is drawn out, pulled toward you.
senses.whyCN: 盒子以动作得名：它被 draw 出来，拉向你。

senses.title: A person who draws
senses.definition: a person who draws pictures or cheques
senses.definitionCN: 画图的人或开出票据的人
senses.example: He is a fine drawer of birds.
senses.exampleCN: 他画鸟画得很好。
senses.why: The -er suffix turns the verb into the doer.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -er 把动词变成动作的执行者。

intro.en: Drawer is simply the thing that is drawn out, named by its action.
intro.cn: drawer 就是「被拉出的东西」，以动作命名。

items.en: Old English dragan meant to pull, the root of draw.
items.cn: 古英语 dragan 意为拉，是 draw 的词根。

items.en: Draw applied to pulling boxes out of chests.
items.cn: 中古英语 draw 被用来指从柜子里拉出匣子。

items.en: Drawer named both the box and the person pulling.
items.cn: drawer 既指匣子，也指拉的人。

items.en: The furniture sense became the everyday one.
items.cn: 家具义成为日常用法。

items.en: Banking still uses drawer for the person who signs a cheque.
items.cn: 银行业仍用 drawer 称开出支票的人。

note.en: These words sit near drawer in form or meaning.
note.cn: 这些词在形式或意义上与 drawer 相邻。

entries.definition: the base verb
a picture
legal adviser, different root
entries.definitionCN: 律师（拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a container with straight sides
furniture with drawers or doors
a flat storage board

normalIntro.en: Remember: a drawer is drawn out.
normalIntro.cn: 记住：drawer 就是被拉出来的。

normal.en: open the drawer: you draw it toward you.
normal.cn: open the drawer：把它朝自己拉。

normal.en: a chest of drawers holds many sliding boxes.
normal.cn: chest of drawers 装着许多滑动的小盒。

normal.en: drawer and draw share the pulling root.
normal.cn: drawer 与 draw 共享拉拽词根。

normal.en: The top drawer is easiest to reach.
normal.cn: 最上层的抽屉最容易够到。

normal.en: A neat drawer saves ten minutes a day.
normal.cn: 整齐的抽屉每天省十分钟。

abstract.en: Feel the small brass handle cool in your fingers.
abstract.cn: 感受黄铜小拉手在指间的凉意。

abstract.en: Hear the wooden runners sliding smooth.
abstract.cn: 听木质滑轨顺滑的滑动声。

abstract.en: See the forgotten eraser smiling from the corner.
abstract.cn: 看角落里被遗忘的橡皮。

examples.en: The passport lives in the second drawer down.
examples.cn: 护照在往下数第二个抽屉里。

examples.en: He cleared the drawer of old receipts.
examples.cn: 他清理了抽屉里的旧收据。

examples.en: Each drawer of the cabinet has a label.
examples.cn: 柜子的每个抽屉都贴了标签。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「桌啊」——抽屉从「桌啊」里被拉出来

root: 由 draw（拉，源自古英语 dragan）加 -er（施动者/受动者后缀）构成，本义「被拉出的东西」，指抽屉。

sensesIntro.en: Drawer is the box you draw out, and, in formal use, the person who draws.
sensesIntro.cn: drawer 是被拉出来的盒子，正式场合也指开出票据的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small sliding box with a brass handle
core.cn: 核心意象：带小拉手的滑动木盒

branches.en: The box pulled open
branches.cn: 被拉开的小盒

branches.en: The hand that draws pictures
branches.cn: 画画的那只手

branches.en: The chest holding many boxes
branches.cn: 装着许多小盒的柜子

branches.en: The signature on a cheque
branches.cn: 支票上的签名

branches.en: From pulling boxes to pulling lines
branches.cn: 从拉盒子到拉线条

intro.en: Drawer lives in the pull-family and the furniture set.
intro.cn: drawer 同时住在「拉拽」词族与「家具」词组里。

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic dragan, to pull.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是日耳曼语 dragan（拉）。

definition_en: the covering on top of a building or vehicle, or to put a cover on top
core_image: 雨中的一片斜屋顶
scene: 雨水从老房子的屋顶漏进屋里。 Rain leaked through the roof of the old house.
sceneCN: 这里 roof 是「屋顶」（第 1 个义项）；句意：雨水从老房子的屋顶漏进屋里。

derivatives.zh: 屋顶材料；盖顶
盖屋顶的工人
无屋顶的

senses.title: Building top
senses.definition: the structure that covers the top of a building
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖在建筑物顶部的结构
senses.example: The wind tore tiles from the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 大风把瓦片从屋顶上刮了下来。
senses.why: The cover closes the house from above.
senses.whyCN: 这层覆盖物从上方把房子盖住。

senses.title: Vehicle top
senses.definition: the top part of a car or other vehicle
senses.definitionCN: 汽车或其他交通工具的顶部
senses.example: They tied the bikes to the roof of the car.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把自行车绑在车顶上。
senses.why: The same covering idea moves to a vehicle.
senses.whyCN: 同样的覆盖概念被移用到车辆上。

senses.title: To cover
senses.definition: to put a roof or cover on a building
senses.definitionCN: 给建筑物加盖屋顶或覆盖物
senses.example: Workers roofed the barn before winter.
senses.exampleCN: 工人在入冬前给谷仓盖好了顶。
senses.why: The noun turns into the act of covering.
senses.whyCN: 名词转成覆盖这一动作。

intro.en: Roof comes from Old English hrof, the cover of a house.
intro.cn: roof 源自古代英语 hrof，意为房屋的覆盖物。

items.en: Hrof names the cover over a building.
items.cn: hrof 指建筑物上方的覆盖物。

items.en: Hrof keeps the same meaning in the north.
items.cn: hrof 在北方语言中保持相同含义。

items.en: Rof settles into the modern spelling.
items.cn: rof 逐渐过渡到现代拼写。

items.en: Roof extends from houses to cars and buses.
items.cn: roof 从房屋扩展到汽车和巴士。

items.en: Roof garden adds the idea of use on top.
items.cn: roof garden 增加了在顶上使用的含义。

note.en: A roof covers a building; a ceiling covers a room.
note.cn: roof 覆盖整栋建筑，ceiling 则覆盖房间内部。

entries.definition: evidence that something is true
the hard foot of a horse
the top surface of a roof
the highest part of something
something placed over an object
the inside top of a room

normalIntro.en: A roof is the cover that sits on top.
normalIntro.cn: roof 是盖在顶上的那层覆盖物。

normal.en: Snow lay thick on the roof.
normal.cn: 屋顶上积了厚厚的雪。

normal.en: They built a roof garden on the flat top.
normal.cn: 他们在平顶上建了屋顶花园。

normal.en: The roof rack holds two bicycles.
normal.cn: 车顶架放着两辆自行车。

normal.en: The whole family lives under one roof.
normal.cn: 一家人住在同一屋檐下。

normal.en: The crowd raised the roof at the concert.
normal.cn: 音乐会上人群喧闹欢腾。

abstract.en: Picture a steep roof shining after rain.
abstract.cn: 想象雨后发亮的陡斜屋顶。

abstract.en: Imagine a hand pulling a cover over a box.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把盖子拉到箱子上。

abstract.en: Think of one wide roof sheltering many people.
abstract.cn: 想象一片宽大的屋顶庇护着许多人。

examples.en: A bird built its nest under the roof.
examples.cn: 一只鸟在屋檐下筑巢。

examples.en: The sun beat down on the car roof.
examples.cn: 烈日晒在车顶上。

examples.en: They roofed the shed with cheap boards.
examples.cn: 他们用便宜木板给棚子盖了顶。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「roof」像「如夫」——像丈夫一样撑在头顶上遮风挡雨的那一层，就是屋顶。

root: 古代英语 hrof（房屋覆盖物）与古诺斯语同源，核心义「盖在顶上的保护层」。

sensesIntro.en: Roof means the cover of a building, the top of a vehicle, or to put such a cover on.
sensesIntro.cn: roof 意为建筑物屋顶、车辆顶部，或给某物加盖顶。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sloped roof in the rain.
core.cn: 核心意象：雨中的斜屋顶。

branches.en: The building cover is the main sense.
branches.cn: 建筑屋顶是主要义项。

branches.en: The vehicle top borrows the same cover.
branches.cn: 车辆顶部借用同样的覆盖概念。

branches.en: The verb names putting the cover on.
branches.cn: 动词指加上覆盖物。

branches.en: Building and covering share one structure.
branches.cn: 建筑与盖顶共享同一结构。

branches.en: Both protect what lies beneath.
branches.cn: 两者都保护下方之物。

intro.en: Roof is an old Germanic word with English compounds.

definition_en: very strange or not sensible; extremely enthusiastic about something
core_image: 头发乱翘、想法乱飞的怪人
scene: 愚人节那天，同桌竟然把橡皮擦当成了面包咬了一口，全班笑翻。 That was a really crazy thing to do.
sceneCN: 这里 crazy 是「疯狂的」（第 1 个义项：不像正常人会做的傻事）；句意是那实在是一件疯狂的事。

derivatives.zh: 由词根 craze 构成，义为「狂热；时尚风潮」

senses.title: Not sensible; very strange
senses.definition: silly or unreasonable in a way that surprises people
senses.definitionCN: 愚蠢或不合常理，让人吃惊
senses.example: It was crazy to swim in the river in December.
senses.exampleCN: 十二月在河里游泳太疯狂了。
senses.why: The core image is a mind that has slipped its tracks, so acts no sane person would choose are crazy.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是头脑脱了轨，所以正常人不会选的行为就是 crazy。

senses.title: Extremely fond of something
senses.definition: liking something so much that it seems to fill your whole mind
senses.definitionCN: 喜欢某物到了它占满整个脑袋的程度
senses.example: Ben is crazy about space movies and watches one every weekend.
senses.exampleCN: 本对太空电影着迷，每个周末都要看一部。
senses.why: The same slipped-track mind now runs only toward one thing, so deep love for a hobby is also crazy.
senses.whyCN: 同样脱轨的头脑现在只朝一个方向跑，所以对爱好的痴迷也可以用 crazy。

senses.title: Wild or out of control
senses.definition: moving, noisy or changing in a wild, uncontrolled way
senses.definitionCN: 以狂乱、失控的方式移动、喧闹或变化
senses.example: The last day before the holiday was crazy at school.
senses.exampleCN: 放假前的最后一天，学校里乱成一团。
senses.why: When many things fly at once, the scene looks like the slipped mind made real, so chaos is crazy too.
senses.whyCN: 当许多事情同时乱飞时，场面就像脱轨头脑的现实版，所以混乱也是 crazy。

intro.en: Crazy grew from an old word that meant to shatter or crack.
intro.cn: crazy 由一个意为「打碎、破裂」的旧词发展而来。

items.en: The Old Norse krasa meant to smash or break, the likely source of the crack idea.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 krasa 意为砸碎、打破，很可能是「破裂」意象的来源。

items.en: English had the verb craze, meaning to shatter or make cracks in pottery.
items.cn: 英语动词 craze 意为打碎，或让陶器产生裂纹。

items.en: Later craze shifted from cracked pots to damaged minds.
items.cn: 后来 craze 从「开裂的陶器」转向「受损的心智」。

items.en: The adjective crazy first meant cracked or frail, then mad.
items.cn: 形容词 crazy 先指开裂易碎的，后指发疯的。

items.en: Today crazy covers silly acts, strong likings and wild scenes.
items.cn: 如今 crazy 覆盖傻事、痴迷和狂乱场面。

note.en: These words share the crack idea or name wild states.
note.cn: 这些词共享「破裂」意象，或表示狂乱状态。

senses.exampleCN: 英语演讲比赛前他感到很有信心。
senses.why: The Latin root means to trust fully, and trusting yourself gives the feeling of confidence.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根本义是完全信任，信任自己便生出自信的感觉。

senses.title: Certain that something is true
senses.definition: being certain that something will happen or is true
senses.definitionCN: 确信某事会发生或是真的
senses.example: The scientists are confident that the plan will work.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家们确信这个计划会成功。
senses.why: The same trust turns outward: when you trust the facts, you are confident about the truth.
senses.whyCN: 同样的信任转向外部：当你相信事实，你便对真相确信不疑。

senses.title: Showing belief in yourself
senses.definition: behaving in a way that shows you believe in yourself
senses.definitionCN: 举止表现出相信自己的样子
senses.example: She walked into the classroom with a confident smile.
senses.exampleCN: 她带着自信的微笑走进教室。
senses.why: Inner belief shows on the outside, so confident also describes a look or manner.
senses.whyCN: 内心的信念会显露在外，所以 confident 也形容神态举止。

intro.en: Confident comes from Latin words meaning to trust fully.
intro.cn: confident 来自拉丁语，本义是「完全信任」。

items.en: The Latin verb confidere meant to trust fully, from con- (fully) + fidere (to trust).
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 confidere 意为完全信任，由 con-（完全）+ fidere（信任）构成。

items.en: The related noun fiducia meant trust, the ancestor of confidence.
items.cn: 相关名词 fiducia 意为信任，是 confidence 的祖先。

items.en: French carried the idea into confident, meaning trusting.
items.cn: 法语把这一概念带入 confident，意为信任的。

items.en: English adopted confident in the fifteenth century, first about trusting people.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪吸收 confident，最初指信任他人。

items.en: Later the meaning moved to self-belief, and confidence became a common noun.
items.cn: 后来词义转向自我信念，confidence 也成了常用名词。

note.en: All these words grow from the Latin root fidere, to trust.
note.cn: 这些词都生长自拉丁词根 fidere（信任）。

entries.definition: the feeling that you can trust someone or something
secret; meant to be kept trusted and private
to tell a secret to someone you trust
a person you trust with your secrets
shy and lacking confidence; the di- prefix turns the meaning around
entries.definitionCN: 羞怯的；缺乏自信的（前缀不同，词义相反）

entries.definition: sure that something is true
not doubting at all
confident and calm
completely sure about something

normalIntro.en: Break the word into con + fid + ent.
normalIntro.cn: 把单词拆成 con 加 fid 加 ent 来记。

normal.en: confident = con- (fully) + fid (trust) + -ent.
normal.cn: confident 由 con-（完全）+ fid（信任）+ -ent 构成。

normal.en: fid is the trust root in confide and confidential.
normal.cn: fid 是信任词根，见于 confide 和 confidential。

normal.en: diffident adds di- (away) and means not confident.
normal.cn: diffident 加 di-（离开）表示不自信。

normal.en: confidence is the noun form of confident.
normal.cn: confidence 是 confident 的名词形式。

normal.en: confident sounds like can-find-ent; you can find your courage.
normal.cn: confident 发音像 can-find-ent，你能找到自己的勇气。

abstract.en: Picture standing tall on the stage with your chin up.
abstract.cn: 想象在台上站得笔直、抬起下巴。

abstract.en: Picture a steady flame that no wind can blow out.
abstract.cn: 想象一支风吹不灭的稳定火苗。

abstract.en: Picture shaking hands firmly before a match.
abstract.cn: 想象赛前坚定地握了握手。

examples.en: I am confident that our team will win the relay race.
examples.cn: 我确信我们队会赢得接力赛。

examples.en: She gave a confident answer in front of the whole class.
examples.cn: 她在全班面前自信地作了回答。

examples.en: Practice every day and you will become more confident in English.
examples.cn: 每天练习，你的英语会越来越有信心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「康非登特」——健康又不怕（非）登台（登）的特（特）长生，上台一点都不怯场。

root: 拉丁语 confidere（完全信任），由 con-（完全）+ fidere（信任）构成。fid 是「信任」词根，同族词有 confide（吐露）、confidential（机密的）。

sensesIntro.en: From trusting yourself to being sure of facts.
sensesIntro.cn: 从相信自己延伸到确信事实。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: trusting fully
core.cn: 核心意象：完全信任

branches.en: Trusting your own ability.
branches.cn: 相信自己的能力。

branches.en: Trusting that facts are true.
branches.cn: 相信事实为真。

branches.en: Belief showing in manner.
branches.cn: 信念显露在举止上。

branches.en: Inner trust becomes outer poise.
branches.cn: 内心的信任变成外在的从容。

branches.en: Certainty colors the way you act.
branches.cn: 确定感影响着行动方式。

intro.en: The fid root of trusting quietly builds a whole word family.
intro.cn: fid（信任）词根悄悄构建出一整个词族。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fidere 意为信任，英语多次借用。

items.exampleCN: 他把全部精力集中在比赛上。

items.example: You must have faith in your teammates.
His confidence grew with every win.
items.exampleCN: 他每赢一场信心就增一分。

definition_en: moving to a position inside something, changing to a new state, or showing direction of attention
core_image: 一支箭正穿过门框，箭头已经进到屋子里面
scene: 孩子端着热汤从厨房走到客厅，小心地跨过门槛。 She walked into the room without knocking.
sceneCN: 这里 into 是「到……里面」（第 1 个义项：向内的移动），句意为她没敲门就走进了房间。画面里的物件：门槛、端着的汤碗、门框。

pos.zh: 介词：到……里面；进入；变成；对……

derivatives.zh: 去掉后缀 to 构成，义为「在……里面」
结构平行的词，义为「到……上面」
功能相近的方位介词，义为「朝向」

senses.title: Movement to the inside
senses.definition: to a position inside a place, container, or space
senses.definitionCN: 到一个地方、容器或空间的里面
senses.example: He poured the milk into a tall glass.
senses.exampleCN: 他把牛奶倒进一只高玻璃杯里。
senses.why: In names the position; to names the movement. Into fuses both in one word.
senses.whyCN: in 表示位置，to 表示移动；into 把两者合成一个词。

senses.title: A change of state
senses.definition: showing the result of a change from one state or form to another
senses.definitionCN: 表示从一种状态或形态变成另一种的结果
senses.example: The water froze into solid ice overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 水一夜之间冻成了坚冰。
senses.why: Change is pictured as entering a new container called a state.
senses.whyCN: 变化被想象成走进一个叫「状态」的新容器。

senses.title: Collision or contact
senses.definition: showing that something strikes or meets something else
senses.definitionCN: 表示某物撞到或遇到另一物
senses.example: The car ran into the fence at the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 汽车在拐角处撞上了栅栏。
senses.why: Running into a thing means moving into the space it fills.
senses.whyCN: run into 某物，就是进入它占据的那块空间。

senses.title: Interest and attention
senses.definition: showing what someone is interested in or is examining closely
senses.definitionCN: 表示某人感兴趣或正在仔细查看的对象
senses.example: She is really into old films these days.
senses.exampleCN: 她最近非常迷老电影。
senses.why: Attention is also movement: the mind goes into whatever it studies.
senses.whyCN: 注意力也是一种移动：心走进它所研究的东西。

intro.en: Into is a native English compound of in and to, first written as two words.
intro.cn: into 是英语本土词，由 in 与 to 合成，最初写作两个词。

items.en: In and to were separate words with separate jobs.
items.cn: in 与 to 是两个各司其职的独立词。

items.en: Writers placed them side by side for movement inward.
items.cn: 写作者把它们并排放在一起表示向内的移动。

items.en: The two were written as one word in the medieval period.
items.cn: 中世纪时期这两个词被写成一个词。

items.en: Into became the standard form for motion and change.
items.cn: into 成为表示移动与变化的标准形式。

items.en: Idioms such as run into and be into widened its range.
items.cn: run into 与 be into 等习语又扩大了它的用法。

note.en: The look-alike group holds other small prepositions of place; the near-meaning group holds older motion words.
note.cn: 形近组收其他表方位的小介词；近义组收较古的移动词。

entries.definition: Position inside, not movement.
entries.definitionCN: 介词义为「在……里面」，表位置。

entries.definition: An archaic form meaning to or toward.
Movement to a position on a surface.
Within the limits of something.
entries.definitionCN: 介词义为「在……之内」，语气更实。

entries.definition: In the direction of, without entering.
entries.definitionCN: 介词义为「朝向」，不含进入。

entries.definition: Inside a space or a period of time.
entries.definitionCN: 介词义为「在……之内」，偏书面。

normalIntro.en: These hooks treat the word as in plus to walking through a door.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把这个词看成 in 加 to 一起穿过一道门。

normal.en: Into is simply in and to run together.
normal.cn: into 就是 in 与 to 并在一起。

normal.en: In is where you are; into is how you got there.
normal.cn: in 是你在哪，into 是你怎么进去的。

normal.en: Change also uses into: ice into water, paper into ash.
normal.cn: 变化也用 into：冰成水、纸成灰。

normal.en: Run into someone means meet them by accident.
normal.cn: run into someone 意思是偶然碰上。

normal.en: Be into a band means the band is where your mind goes.
normal.cn: be into a band 意思是心都往那支乐队里去。

abstract.en: Into is a word shaped like a doorway.
abstract.cn: into 是一个长得像门口的词。

abstract.en: Every change of state is a small migration inward.
abstract.cn: 每一次状态转变都是一次向内的迁徙。

abstract.en: We fall into habits as easily as into chairs.
abstract.cn: 我们掉进习惯，就像落进椅子那么自然。

examples.en: The cat slipped into the box and refused to come out.
examples.cn: 猫钻进箱子，怎么也不肯出来。

examples.en: The argument turned into a long silence.
examples.cn: 那场争论最后变成了长久的沉默。

examples.en: He is into repairing old bicycles.
examples.cn: 他很热衷于修旧自行车。

root: 古英语 in「在内」+ to「向」→ 中世纪合写为 into，表示向内的移动与状态变化。同族有 in、inside、unto。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: motion inside, change of state, collision, and direction of interest.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：向内的移动、状态变化、相撞，以及兴趣所指。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an arrow already halfway through a doorway.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支箭已穿过门框一半。

branches.en: THE CUP: liquid moving to the inside of a container.
branches.cn: 杯子这条线：液体移进容器内部。

branches.en: THE ICE: one state becoming another.
branches.cn: 冰这条线：一种状态变成另一种。

branches.en: THE FENCE: a moving thing meets a solid thing.
branches.cn: 栅栏这条线：运动之物撞上实体。

branches.en: THE RECORD: attention travelling to a favourite subject.
branches.cn: 唱片这条线：注意力移向偏爱的主题。

branches.en: THE LINK: both read an abstract space as a room to enter.
branches.cn: 连接线：两者都把抽象空间当成可进的房间。

intro.cn: into 没有拉丁成分：它是本土的 in 接上 to。

items.example: It names the direction of travel.
The compound carries both ideas at once.
items.exampleCN: 这个合成词同时带着两个意思。

items.example: The same pattern with on instead of in.
items.exampleCN: 同一结构，把 in 换成 on。

items.example: An older form that lost ground.
It names the inner space itself.
items.exampleCN: 它指里面那块空间本身。

items.example: It keeps the direction without the entry.

items.exampleCN: 它是 in 的书面表亲。

definition_zh: 镜子；镜面；写照；反映；映照
definition_en: a piece of glass with a reflective coating that shows images; also something that gives a faithful picture of a situation, and to show or match something as a mirror does
core_image: 晨光里的一面镜子，把窗前的人原样照回来
scene: 清晨的走廊上，她把外套领子翻正，又抬手理了理头发。 She checked her collar in the mirror before the interview.
sceneCN: 这里是「镜子」（第 1 个义项：能照出影像的玻璃物件）；句意为面试前她对着镜子整理衣领。图中可辨识物件：镜子、衣领、走廊灯。

derivatives.zh: 由动词 mirror 加 -ing 构成，义为「镜像；反映」
由动词 mirror 加 -ed 构成，义为「装有镜子的；映出的」
由 mirror 加表示「没有」的 -less 构成，义为「无镜的」，多指相机结构

senses.title: A glass surface that shows a reflection
senses.definition: a piece of glass or polished surface with a reflective coating that shows the image of what stands before it
senses.definitionCN: 镀有反光层的玻璃或抛光表面，能照出面前事物的影像
senses.example: She checked her collar in the mirror before the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 面试前她对着镜子整理衣领。
senses.why: The word came through Old French from a Vulgar Latin noun for a looking glass, built on the verb mirari, to look at or wonder at, so the object is named for the gaze it invites.
senses.whyCN: 这个词经古法语来自一个表示「照人用的玻璃」的俗拉丁名词，后者建于动词 mirari（注视、惊叹）之上，所以物件是按它招来的那道目光命名的。

senses.title: A faithful picture of a situation
senses.definition: a person or thing that shows a situation, a period or a mood exactly as it is
senses.definitionCN: 把某种局面、时代或情绪如实呈现出来的人或事物
senses.example: The novel is a mirror of its age.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说是那个时代的写照。
senses.why: Because a mirror returns an exact image rather than a flattering one, writers use it for anything that shows a situation without distortion, and a novel can serve as that surface.
senses.whyCN: 镜子给出的是准确而非讨好的影像，作家便用它指任何不失真地呈现局面的东西，一部小说也能充当这样一面镜面。

senses.title: To show an image as a mirror does
senses.definition: to show the image of something, the way a still surface reflects what stands beside it
senses.definitionCN: 像平静表面那样把旁边的事物影像呈现出来
senses.example: The lake mirrored the pines along the shore.
senses.exampleCN: 湖面映出岸边的松树。
senses.why: The verb was simply the noun turned into an action, so to mirror is to do what a mirror does: send back the image of whatever stands before it.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词就是把名词直接变成动作，所以 to mirror 就是做镜子所做的事：把面前事物的影像送回原处。

senses.title: To match or correspond closely
senses.definition: to be very similar to something else, so that the two seem to copy each other
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事物极为相似，看上去像彼此复制出来的一样
senses.example: The vote mirrored the national trend.
senses.exampleCN: 投票结果与全国趋势一致。
senses.why: When two patterns look identical, one seems to be the reflection of the other, so the verb widened from reflecting light to reflecting behaviour, numbers and opinions.
senses.whyCN: 当两种走势看起来一模一样，其中一个就像是另一个的倒影，于是这个动词从映出光线扩展到映出行为、数字与观点。

intro.en: Mirror comes from a Vulgar Latin name for a looking glass, built on the verb mirari, to look at or wonder at, and it reached English through Old French.
intro.cn: mirror 来自俗拉丁语中「照人用的玻璃」这一名称，建立在动词 mirari（注视、惊叹）之上，再经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Mirari meant to look at with wonder, and the looking and the wondering were not separated in the verb.
items.cn: mirari 意为带着惊叹地看，在这个动词里，「看」与「惊叹」并没有分开。

items.en: A Vulgar Latin noun, reconstructed as miratorium, named the thing one looks into; the form is a reconstruction rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: 俗拉丁语中有一个表示「供人照看的器物」的名词，学界重构为 miratorium；这是重构形式，并非有记录的词。

items.en: Old French mirour carried the noun into ordinary use for the polished metal or glass a person looks into.
items.cn: 古法语 mirour 把这个名词带入日常用法，指人们照看的抛光金属或玻璃。

items.en: Middle English mirrour kept the extra vowel of the French form and also used the word for moral examples and ideal portraits.
items.cn: 中古英语的 mirrour 保留了法语形式里多出的元音，也用这个词指道德榜样与理想化的画像。

items.en: Modern English shortened the spelling to mirror, formed a matching verb, and pushed the word into talk about trends, reports and behaviour.
items.cn: 现代英语把拼写缩成 mirror，造出与之相配的动词，并把这个词推进到关于趋势、报告与行为的说法里。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin verb for looking and wondering; the near-meaning group gathers words for reflections and for the surfaces that produce them.
note.cn: 形近组顺着拉丁语中表示「看」与「惊叹」的动词展开；近义组收表示影像以及产生影像的表面的词。

entries.definition: An optical illusion in which water seems to appear in the distance.
entries.definitionCN: 远处看似有水的一种光学幻景。

entries.definition: To look at someone with wonder and approval.
entries.definitionCN: 带着惊叹与赞许地看某人。

entries.definition: An astonishing event believed to come from divine power.
entries.definitionCN: 被认为是神力所致的惊人之事。

entries.definition: The act of reflecting an image, or of copying another's behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 映出影像的行为，或模仿他人行为的过程。

entries.definition: The image of something seen in a mirror or on water.
entries.definitionCN: 镜中或水面看到的事物的影像。

entries.definition: A hard, transparent material, or a mirror made from it.
entries.definitionCN: 坚硬透明的材料，或用它制成的镜子。

entries.definition: A picture or likeness of someone or something.
entries.definitionCN: 某人某物的图像或相似物。

entries.definition: To send back light or an image, or to show a situation.
entries.definitionCN: 把光或影像送回；反映某种情况。

normalIntro.en: The Latin verb for looking and wondering gives the noun, and the noun then turns into a verb, so the family keeps moving between the glass and the act of copying.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示「看」与「惊叹」的动词生出名词，名词又变成动词，于是词族在镜面与复制这个动作之间来回移动。

normal.en: Mirari means to look at with wonder, and a mirror was first a looking glass, so the object is named for the gaze it invites.
normal.cn: mirari 意为带着惊叹地看，而 mirror 起初就是照人的玻璃，所以这个物件按它招来的目光得名。

normal.en: Mirror, miracle, mirage and admire share that Latin verb, which is why looking and wondering sit close together in this family.
normal.cn: mirror、miracle、mirage 与 admire 共用那个拉丁动词，所以看与惊叹在这个词族里挨得很近。

normal.en: The noun came first, and to mirror is a later verb made by simply treating the object as an action.
normal.cn: 名词先出现，to mirror 是后来把这个物件直接当作动作来用才有的动词。

normal.en: Mirror image names a copy reversed left to right, the most literal use of the noun in front of another noun.
normal.cn: mirror image 指左右颠倒的复制影像，是名词放在另一个名词前最字面的用法。

normal.en: The phrase a mirror of the times still demands a faithful picture, not a flattering one.
normal.cn: a mirror of the times 这一说法仍然要求如实呈现，而不是美化。

abstract.en: Picture a still lake at dawn returning the trees exactly, without adding or hiding anything.
abstract.cn: 想象黎明时平静的湖面把树影原样送回，既不增添也不隐藏。

abstract.en: A mirror can flatter or accuse, but it cannot lie about the shape in front of it; the word keeps that demand for accuracy.
abstract.cn: 镜子可以讨好也可以揭短，但它无法对面前的形状说谎；这个词一直保留着这份准确的要求。

abstract.en: To mirror someone is to become their reflection, which is why imitation and understanding can look the same from outside.
abstract.cn: to mirror 某人就是成为他的倒影，所以模仿与理解从外面看往往一模一样。

examples.en: She checked her collar in the mirror.
examples.cn: 她对着镜子整理衣领。

examples.en: The lake mirrored the pines along the shore.
examples.cn: 湖面映出岸边的松树。

examples.en: The report mirrors what workers have been saying for years.
examples.cn: 这份报告反映了工人们多年来的说法。

definition_en: to speak or write about something briefly; also a short reference, a formal naming for praise, or a phrase that adds a stronger point
core_image: 一个人说话时顺手把某件事轻轻带过，只用半句话点到
scene: 会议开到一半，有人问起预算，负责人只在纸上写了一行小字。 At the meeting she mentioned the budget only once, then moved on.
sceneCN: 这里是「提到、说起」（第 1 个义项：口头或书面简短提及）；句意为她在会上只提了一次预算，随后就继续往下说。图中可辨识物件：会议桌、纸笔、写着一行小字的便笺。

derivatives.zh: 由 mention 加 -able 构成，义为「值得一提的」

senses.title: To refer to something briefly
senses.definition: to say or write something about someone or something, without going into detail
senses.definitionCN: 简短地说到或写到某人或某事，不作详细展开
senses.example: She mentioned your name at the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 她在会上提到了你的名字。
senses.why: The Latin noun mentio is a calling to mind; to mention something is to bring it into the listener's mind for a moment, not to dwell on it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语名词 mentio 本义是「唤起心中的记忆」；mention 一件事，就是把它在听者心里唤起来一小会儿，而不是停下来细讲。

senses.title: A brief reference
senses.definition: a short remark or written reference to someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某事的简短评论或书面提及
senses.example: There was no mention of the price in the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 信里没有提到价格。
senses.why: Once the verb names the act, the noun can name the act itself as a thing: a mention is the small trace the act leaves in speech or text.
senses.whyCN: 动词既然指「提到」这个动作，名词就可以把动作本身当成一件事来指：a mention 就是这一动作在话语或文字里留下的一点小痕迹。

senses.title: To name someone for praise
senses.definition: to name a person formally, especially in a military report, as deserving recognition
senses.definitionCN: 正式点出某人的名字以示表彰，尤指在军方报告中
senses.example: The officer was mentioned in dispatches for his conduct.
senses.exampleCN: 这名军官因表现突出在战报中受到嘉奖。
senses.why: A formal report lists names one by one; naming a person in that list is a kind of mention, so the word comes to mean official recognition.
senses.whyCN: 正式报告会逐个列出名字；把某人写进这份名单，本身就是一种 mention，于是这个词引申为官方表彰。

senses.title: An added point that strengthens the statement
senses.definition: used to introduce a further fact that makes what has just been said stronger
senses.definitionCN: 用来引出更进一步的事实，使刚说过的话更有分量
senses.example: He speaks three languages, not to mention his fluent Chinese.
senses.exampleCN: 他会说三种语言，更不用说他那口流利的中文了。
senses.why: The phrase not to mention began as a way of saying 'without even speaking of', and it turned a bare mention into a rhetorical upgrade.
senses.whyCN: 短语 not to mention 起初表示「连说都不用说」，于是把一个轻描淡写的提及变成了加强语气的修辞手段。

intro.en: Mention comes from a Latin noun for calling something to mind, and its history keeps the idea of the mind rather than the mouth.
intro.cn: mention 来自拉丁语中表示「把某事唤到心上」的名词，它的历史始终围绕「心」而不是「嘴」。

items.en: Mentio meant a mentioning or a calling to mind, and it was formed on the root of mens, the mind.
items.cn: mentio 意为「提及、唤到心上」，由表示「心」的 mens 词根构成。

items.en: Mens named the mind or the thinking faculty; the same root produced memini, I remember, and memor, mindful.
items.cn: mens 指心智或思考能力；同一词根还产生 memini（我记得）与 memor（记着的）。

items.en: Old French took the Latin noun as mention and used it for a spoken or written reference.
items.cn: 古法语把这一拉丁名词写作 mention，用于口头或书面的提及。

items.en: Middle English used mention as both noun and verb, and the verb soon became the everyday way to point at a topic.
items.cn: 中古英语中 mention 既作名词也作动词，动词很快成为点出一个话题的日常说法。

items.en: Modern English fixed the phrase not to mention and the military sense of being mentioned in dispatches.
items.cn: 现代英语固定了 not to mention 这一说法，以及「在战报中受到嘉奖」的军事义。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that share the Latin mind-root or merely resemble the spelling; the near-meaning group collects verbs for pointing at a topic.
note.cn: 形近组收共享拉丁「心」词根或只是拼写相像的词；近义组收表示「点出话题」的动词。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin noun for memory and a root for mind; its family keeps speaking tied to thinking.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在表示记忆的拉丁名词与表示心智的词根上，同族词始终把「说」和「想」系在一起。

normal.en: Mentio in Latin is a calling to mind, so a mention brings a topic into the listener's head rather than into the centre of the talk.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 mentio 是「唤到心上」，所以 mention 是把话题送进听者脑中，而不是摆到谈话中心。

normal.en: The root mens means mind, and mental still carries that meaning, which is why a mention is a mental event before it is a spoken one.
normal.cn: 词根 mens 意为心智，mental 至今保留此义，所以 mention 先是心里的事，然后才是嘴里的事。

normal.en: Mentioned in dispatches is a fixed military phrase: the name is written into a report, and writing a name is a literal mention.
normal.cn: mentioned in dispatches 是固定的军事说法：名字被写进报告，而写下一个名字就是字面意义上的 mention。

normal.en: Not to mention works like a hinge: it adds a stronger fact after a weaker one.
normal.cn: not to mention 像一扇铰链：先给一个较轻的事实，再挂上一个更重的。

normal.en: The noun and the verb share one spelling, so mention can be the act or the short reference it produces.
normal.cn: 名词与动词同形，所以 mention 既可以是「提到」这个动作，也可以是动作留下的那句短话。

abstract.en: Picture a finger tapping one word on a long page and then moving on; that tap is a mention.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指在长页面上轻点一个词，然后继续移动；那一点就是 mention。

abstract.en: A mention is a small door: it lets a topic in without letting it take over the room.
abstract.cn: mention 是一扇小门：它让话题进来，却不让话题占满整个房间。

abstract.en: The word ties speech to memory, because what is mentioned is meant to stay in the mind afterwards.
abstract.cn: 这个词把说话和记忆系在一起，因为被提到的东西本来就是为了留在心里。

sceneCN: 这里 upon 是「在……之上」（第 1 个义项：接触并覆在某物上）；句意为他把手放在封面上，沉默了好一会儿。手掌落上桌面的画面，正是这个词的核心。

senses.title: Resting on a surface
senses.definition: in contact with the top of something
senses.definitionCN: 与某个物体的上表面接触
senses.example: He set the cup upon the table.
senses.exampleCN: 他把杯子放在桌面上。
senses.why: The word is a strengthened form of on, and the physical contact with a surface is its first sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 on 的加强形式，与表面的实物接触是它的第一层意思。

senses.title: Immediately after something happens
senses.definition: at the moment of, or right after, an event
senses.definitionCN: 在某个事件发生之时或紧接其后
senses.example: Upon hearing the news, she dropped the phone.
senses.exampleCN: 一听到消息，她就把电话掉了。
senses.why: Whatever lies upon something arrives touching it at once, and this contact becomes immediate succession.
senses.whyCN: 放在某物之上的东西会立刻贴上它，这种接触便化为「紧接而来」。

senses.title: Used for the basis of a decision
senses.definition: used to introduce what a decision or belief rests on
senses.definitionCN: 用于引出决定或信念所依托之物
senses.example: The judge acted upon the evidence in the file.
senses.exampleCN: 法官依据卷宗里的证据行事。
senses.why: A decision resting on evidence is like a weight resting on a table, so the word marks the ground beneath it.
senses.whyCN: 决定依托证据，就像重物托在桌面上，于是这个词用来标出底下的那块地面。

senses.title: Used in formal statements of obligation
senses.definition: used to name who carries a duty or a blame
senses.definitionCN: 用于指明义务或过失由谁承担
senses.example: The duty fell upon the youngest son.
senses.exampleCN: 这份责任落在了最小的儿子身上。
senses.why: A duty set on a person is literally a load placed on a surface, and the image transfers to responsibility.
senses.whyCN: 落在某人身上的义务，字面上就是压在某个表面上的一份重量，于是这个画面转成了责任。

senses.title: Frozen in story openings
senses.definition: kept in the fixed phrase that begins folk tales
senses.definitionCN: 保留在童话开头固定说法里
senses.example: Once upon a time a shop stood on this corner.
senses.exampleCN: 从前这个街角开着一家店。
senses.why: The tale's first scene is placed upon a time, and the phrase has not changed for centuries.
senses.whyCN: 故事的第一个场景被「搁在」一段时间上，这个说法几百年都没变。

items.en: On is ancient, and up is an old adverb of motion upward.

items.en: The compound uppon puts the two together with the sense of resting on top of.
items.cn: 复合形式 uppon 把两者合起来，意为「覆于其上」。

items.en: Upon competes with on and keeps a more formal and literary tone.
items.cn: upon 与 on 并用，但保留了更正式、更书卷的语气。

items.en: Upon fixes itself in set phrases such as once upon a time and upon request.
items.cn: upon 固定在 once upon a time、upon request 等熟语里。

items.en: The sense of immediately after develops in formal writing.

normalIntro.en: A piled-up preposition, formal in tone, alive mostly in fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 一个叠加而成的介词，语气正式，主要活在固定短语里。

normal.en: Think of upon as on with an extra push of up.
normal.cn: 把 upon 想成 on 加上 up 的一推。

normal.en: Once upon a time is the phrase every learner already knows.
normal.cn: once upon a time 是学习者早已会说的短语。

normal.en: Upon request and upon arrival show the formal register.
normal.cn: upon request 与 upon arrival 显示出正式语气。

normal.en: Rely upon and depend upon are equally correct with on.
normal.cn: rely upon、depend upon 与用 on 一样正确。

normal.en: Upon hearing is the common frame for immediately after.
normal.cn: upon hearing 是表示「一听到就」的常见框架。

abstract.en: Press a palm flat on a book cover.
abstract.cn: 把掌心平平按在书封上。

abstract.en: See one stone laid exactly on another.
abstract.cn: 看一块石头正好压在另一块上。

abstract.en: Hear a door open the instant a knock ends.
abstract.cn: 听敲门声一停，门就开了。

examples.en: She placed the letter upon the desk and turned away.
examples.cn: 她把信放在桌上，转身走了。

examples.en: Upon arriving at the station, he called his mother.
examples.cn: 一到车站，他就给母亲打了电话。

examples.en: The committee decided upon the plan after a long debate.
examples.cn: 经过长时间辩论，委员会就这个方案作出了决定。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额碰」——低头太急，额碰在桌沿上，正好碰在桌面这个「之上」的位置。

root: 古英语复合形式 uppon，由 up（向上）与 on（在……上）合并而成，本义「覆于其上」，与 on 同源同义而语气更正式

sensesIntro.en: Contact with a surface gives rest, then immediate succession, then grounds, then duty, then a story opening.
sensesIntro.cn: 与表面的接触先给「搁置」，再给「紧接」，再给依据、义务，最后给故事开头。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a palm pressed flat on a surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手掌平压在表面上。

branches.en: The surface branch: a thing set down and in contact.
branches.cn: 表面分支：放下去并贴着的东西。

branches.en: The time branch: contact becomes immediate succession.
branches.cn: 时间分支：接触变成紧接其后。

branches.en: The ground branch: what a decision stands on.
branches.cn: 根据分支：决定所踩的地面。

branches.en: The duty branch: blame resting on someone.
branches.cn: 义务分支：落在某人身上的责任。

branches.en: The story branch: the fixed opening of a tale.
branches.cn: 故事分支：故事固定的开头。

intro.en: A compound preposition whose two parts are both very old and still in daily use.
intro.cn: 一个复合介词，两个部分都非常古老，且今天仍在使用。

latinIntro.en: Latin uses super for on top of and in plus a noun for the time sense.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 super 表示「在……之上」，时间义则用 in 加名词。

items.example: The book is on the desk.
Upon arrival, report to the desk.
Once upon a time a girl lived here.
items.exampleCN: 从前有个姑娘住在这里。

items.example: We rely upon the river for water.

definition_zh: 乐队；带子；波段；一伙人；用带子绑；联合
definition_en: a group of musicians, or a thin flat strip used to tie or fasten things
core_image: 一条布带把一捆木棍紧紧束在一起
scene: 学校礼堂里，乐队奏响了第一首歌，台下立刻安静下来。 The band played three songs at the school concert.
sceneCN: 这里 band 是「乐队」（第 1 个义项：一起演奏的一群音乐人）；句意为乐队在学校音乐会上演奏了三首歌。

pos.zh: 名词：乐队；带子；波段；一伙人

derivatives.zh: 由 head 与 band 组合而成，义为「发带、头带」
由 waist 与 band 组合而成，义为「腰带、腰头」
由 band 与 width 组合而成，义为「带宽」
由 band 与 stand 组合而成，义为「露天音乐台」

senses.title: A group of musicians
senses.definition: a small group of people who play music together
senses.definitionCN: 一起演奏音乐的一小群人
senses.example: The band played three songs at the school concert.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队在学校音乐会上演奏了三首歌。
senses.why: A band first meant a company of people bound together, so a group of musicians bound by playing is a natural extension.
senses.whyCN: band 本指被束在一起的一伙人，所以因演奏而聚在一起的一群音乐人是很自然的引申。

senses.title: A thin strip
senses.definition: a thin flat strip of material used to tie, fasten, or decorate something
senses.definitionCN: 用来捆扎、固定或装饰的细长扁条
senses.example: He tied the pencils with a rubber band.
senses.exampleCN: 他用橡皮筋把铅笔捆在一起。
senses.why: The oldest sense is the physical strip that binds things, and that image lies under all the others.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是那条把东西束起来的实物流，它下面的所有义项都从这一形象长出。

senses.title: A range of radio waves
senses.definition: a particular range of frequencies used for radio or other signals
senses.definitionCN: 用于无线电或其他信号的特定频率范围
senses.example: This radio can receive the short-wave band.
senses.exampleCN: 这台收音机能接收短波波段。
senses.why: A strip of the frequency scale is imagined as a strip of material, so a range of waves becomes a band.
senses.whyCN: 频率刻度上的一段被想象成一条带子，于是一段波的范围也叫 band。

senses.title: A group of people
senses.definition: a group of people who share an activity, sometimes with a bad purpose
senses.definitionCN: 因共同活动聚在一起的一群人，有时带贬义
senses.example: A band of thieves broke into the shop at night.
senses.exampleCN: 一伙盗贼夜里闯进了商店。
senses.why: People tied by a common purpose are like things tied by a strip, which gives the group sense.
senses.whyCN: 被共同目的束在一起的人，就像被带子捆住的物件，于是有了「一伙人」的义项。

senses.title: To tie or unite
senses.definition: to fasten something with a band, or to join together for a common aim
senses.definitionCN: 用带子捆住某物，或为共同目标联合起来
senses.example: The villagers banded together to repair the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 村民们联合起来修桥。
senses.why: The verb is the strip in action: putting the band around something, or making a group into one bound unit.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是那条带子在起作用：把带子绕上去，或把一群人束成一个整体。

intro.en: Band comes from a Germanic root meaning to bind, and entered English through both Norse and French.
intro.cn: band 来自表示「捆绑」的日耳曼语词根，经诺尔斯语与法语两条路径进入英语。

items.en: The Germanic verb meaning to bind is the distant root of the word.
items.cn: 表示「捆绑」的日耳曼语动词是这个词的远源。

items.en: Old Norse band meant a cord or a band that fastens something.
items.cn: 古诺尔斯语 band 指用来捆扎的绳或带。

items.en: Old French bande meant a strip and also a troop of people, and reinforced both senses in English.
items.cn: 古法语 bande 既指带子，也指一队人，这两个义项都强化了英语中的用法。

items.en: Middle English used band for a strip of material and for a group of people.
items.cn: 中古英语中用 band 指一条材料，也指一群人。

items.en: The musical sense grows from the idea of a company of players, and the radio sense from a strip of the frequency scale.
items.cn: 音乐义从「一队演奏者」发展而来，无线电义则来自频率刻度上的一条「带」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds built on band; the near-meaning group gathers strips, groups, and musical teams.
note.cn: 形近组收由 band 构成的复合词；近义组收带子、群体与音乐团队。

entries.definition: A strip of cloth used to cover a wound; it comes from the same strip word through French.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「绷带」，经法语来自同一个表示「带子」的词。

entries.definition: A band worn around the head.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「发带、头带」，由 head 与 band 组合而成。

entries.definition: The strip of cloth around the waist of a garment.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「腰头、腰带部分」，由 waist 与 band 组合而成。

entries.definition: The range of frequencies a signal uses, or the amount of data a connection can carry.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「带宽」，指信号占用的频率范围或连接的数据容量。

entries.definition: A long narrow piece of material; it matches the second sense without the binding idea.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「条、带」，对应第二个义项，但不含「捆扎」的意思。

entries.definition: A narrow decorative band of cloth, often tied in a bow.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「丝带、缎带」，多用于装饰，常打成蝴蝶结。

entries.definition: A number of people or things together; the general word for the fourth sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「群、组」，是第四个义项的一般说法。

entries.definition: A large group of musicians led by a conductor; larger and more formal than a band.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「管弦乐团」，规模比 band 更大、更正式。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real root meaning to bind, the compounds, and the everyday phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用词根「捆绑」的真实含义、复合词，以及这个词的日常搭配。

normal.en: The root means to bind, so a band is first the strip that ties things together.
normal.cn: 词根意为「捆绑」，所以 band 最初就是把东西捆在一起的带子。

normal.en: A rubber band stretches around a bundle and holds it, which shows the original image.
normal.cn: 橡皮筋绕着捆扎物一撑，就把它箍住，这正是最初的意象。

normal.en: A band of musicians is a group bound by playing together, not by a physical strip.
normal.cn: 乐队是因一起演奏而束在一起的一群人，并不是被实物带子捆住。

normal.en: Band together keeps the verb sense of tying people into one group.
normal.cn: band together 保留了把人「束」成一个群体的动词义。

normal.en: A radio band is a strip cut out of the whole range of frequencies.
normal.cn: 无线电波段就是从整个频率范围里切出来的一条。

abstract.en: Picture one cloth strip around a bundle of sticks: the sticks stay together because something goes around them.
abstract.cn: 想象一条布带绕住一捆木棍：木棍能聚在一起，是因为有东西绕在它们外面。

abstract.en: The same going-around appears in a wedding band, a headband, and a band of people standing together.
abstract.cn: 同样的「绕一圈」也出现在婚戒、发带和站在一起的一伙人身上。

abstract.en: English lets the strip become a range of waves, because both are long narrow pieces of a larger whole.
abstract.cn: 英语让这条带子变成一段波段，因为两者都是从更大整体里切出的狭长部分。

examples.en: The band played three songs at the school concert.
examples.cn: 乐队在学校音乐会上演奏了三首歌。

examples.en: He tied the pencils with a rubber band.
examples.cn: 他用橡皮筋把铅笔捆在一起。

examples.en: The villagers banded together to repair the bridge.
examples.cn: 村民们联合起来修桥。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「绑的」——一伙人被一条带子绑在一起：乐队、带子

root: band 来自日耳曼语中表示「捆绑」的词根，经古诺尔斯语 band「绳带」与古法语 bande「带子、一队人」进入英语。由「捆扎的带子」引申出「一伙人」「乐队」，又由「一条」引申出「波段」。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of band all start from one strip that binds: the strip itself, the people bound into a group, the musicians bound by playing, a strip of radio frequencies, and the act of tying or uniting.
sensesIntro.cn: band 的五个义项都从一条起捆绑作用的带子出发：带子本身、被束成一伙的人、因演奏而聚的乐队、频率上的一个波段，以及捆绑或联合的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one cloth strip is wound around a bundle of sticks and pulled tight.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条布带绕住一捆木棍，被拉紧。

branches.en: THE STRIP: the oldest sense is the flat piece of material itself.
branches.cn: 带子线：最古老的义项就是那条扁平的实物。

branches.en: THE MUSIC: players bound together by a shared performance form a band.
branches.cn: 音乐线：因共同演出而聚在一起的演奏者构成乐队。

branches.en: THE WAVES: a narrow strip cut from the frequency scale is also a band.
branches.cn: 波段线：从频率刻度上切出的狭长一段也叫 band。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE: people tied by one purpose become a band, sometimes a band of thieves.
branches.cn: 人群线：被同一目的束在一起的人成为一伙，有时是盗贼一伙。

branches.en: THE ACT: the verb puts the strip around something or unites people into one body.
branches.cn: 动作线：动词把带子绕上去，或把人联合成一个整体。

intro.en: Band is a short Germanic root that forms compounds freely, with band as the first or second element.
intro.cn: band 是简短的日耳曼语词根，构词自由，可作复合词的前项或后项。

latinIntro.en: No Latin cognate is recorded for this Germanic root, so the Latin list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个日耳曼语词根没有记录在案的拉丁同族词，因此拉丁词条留空。

items.example: The band around the box was loose.

items.exampleCN: 它与 band 构成 headband。
它与 band 构成 waistband。
它与 band 构成 bandwidth。
它与 band 构成 bandstand。
它由 band 构成 bands。
它由 band 构成 banded。
它与 band 构成 band together。

definition_zh: 结冰；冻结；冷冻；使结冰；（因恐惧）呆住；冻结（资产、价格）
definition_en: to become or make something hard with cold; to stop moving or stay still from fear
core_image: 水在一夜寒风里骤然定住：流动被按了暂停键
scene: 冬夜过后，清晨的池塘铺上了一层薄冰，鸭子的爪印都印在冰面上。 The pond began to freeze during the cold night.
sceneCN: 这里 freeze 是「结冰」的意思（第 1 个义项：液体因低温变硬）；寒夜里池塘水面开始冻结。

derivatives.zh: freeze 加 -er，义为「冰柜；冷冻箱」
现在分词作形容词，义为「极冷的；冰点以下的」
过去分词作形容词，义为「冰冻的；冷冻的」
anti- + freeze，义为「防冻液」

senses.title: To become hard with cold
senses.definition: to turn from liquid into ice at or below zero degrees
senses.definitionCN: 液体在零度或以下变成冰。
senses.example: The river freezes in December every year.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河每年十二月结冰。
senses.why: The Germanic root freusan meant to burn cold, an image of cold striking like fire.
senses.whyCN: 日耳曼词根 freusan 意为「被寒冷灼伤」，把严寒比作火。

senses.title: To make food very cold for keeping
senses.definition: to put food in a freezer to keep it fresh
senses.definitionCN: 把食物放进冰柜低温保存。
senses.example: Mum froze the extra dumplings for next week.
senses.exampleCN: 妈妈把多余的饺子冻起来下周吃。
senses.why: Stopping time for food by stopping its movement.
senses.whyCN: 让食物停止流动，从而停止「变质的时间」。

senses.title: To stop moving from fear or shock
senses.definition: to suddenly stop moving because of fear, shock, or surprise
senses.definitionCN: 因恐惧、震惊而突然停止动作。
senses.example: The rabbit froze in the headlights.
senses.exampleCN: 兔子在车灯下僵住了。
senses.why: Cold strikes a person and body stops like frozen water.
senses.whyCN: 寒冷袭人，身体像冻住的水一样静止。

senses.title: To fix prices or money in place
senses.definition: to officially stop prices, wages, or accounts from changing
senses.definitionCN: 官方停止价格、工资或账户的变动。
senses.example: The city froze bus fares for two years.
senses.exampleCN: 该市把公交票价冻结了两年。
senses.why: Social numbers stop moving just like water in ice.
senses.whyCN: 社会的数字像冰中的水一样停止流动。

intro.en: Freeze comes from an old Germanic root that described cold as a kind of burning.
intro.cn: freeze 出自一个古老的日耳曼词根，它把严寒描述为一种「灼烧」。

items.en: The reconstructed root *freusan meant to burn with cold, shared with frost.
items.cn: 重构词根 *freusan 意为「被寒冷灼伤」，与 frost 同源。

items.en: Freosan meant to congeal or turn into ice.
items.cn: 古英语 freosan 意为凝固、变成冰。

items.en: The frost family kept the root in weather words.
items.cn: frost 一族在气象词中保留了该词根。

items.en: The strong verb forms froze and frozen settled down.
items.cn: 强变化动词形式 froze、frozen 定型。

items.en: Food freezing, financial freezing, and the fear sense all became common.
items.cn: 食品冷冻、金融冻结与恐惧义都在现代英语中普及。

note.en: Words shaped like freeze and words of cold and stillness.
note.cn: 与 freeze 形近的词及表示寒冷、静止的词。

entries.definition: the verb form of free; one letter from freeze
entries.definitionCN: free 的三单形式；与 freeze 仅差一个字母。

entries.definition: thin ice formed on surfaces; shares the Germanic root
entries.definitionCN: 霜；与 freeze 同出日耳曼词根。

entries.definition: a light wind; rhymes with freeze
entries.definitionCN: 微风；与 freeze 押韵，词义无关。

entries.definition: to make cold but not frozen
entries.definitionCN: 使变凉；不到结冰的程度。

entries.definition: to cover with a layer of ice
entries.definitionCN: 结冰覆盖；与 freeze over 近义。

entries.definition: to stop moving and become rigid
entries.definitionCN: 变僵硬；与 freeze 的呆住义近义。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on cold, time-stopping, and the fear sense of freeze.
normalIntro.cn: 围绕寒冷、时间暂停与恐惧义的五条记忆钩子。

normal.en: Water freezes at zero degrees: the flow stops.
normal.cn: 水在零度结冰：流动停止。

normal.en: Freeze, froze, frozen: a strong verb with an o-family.
normal.cn: freeze 的强变化：freeze、froze、frozen。

normal.en: A freezer keeps food by freezing time for it.
normal.cn: 冰柜靠冻结时间来保鲜。

normal.en: Fear freezes bodies as winter freezes rivers.
normal.cn: 恐惧冻结身体，如同寒冬冻结河流。

normal.en: Frost and freeze share the same old root of burning cold.
normal.cn: frost 与 freeze 同根，都指「灼人的冷」。

abstract.en: Picture a lake stopping mid-wave overnight.
abstract.cn: 想象湖面在夜里的波浪半途凝住。

abstract.en: Picture a rabbit rooted still in car lights.
abstract.cn: 想象车灯下僵立不动的兔子。

abstract.en: Picture a price tag nailed to the shelf for two years.
abstract.cn: 想象被钉在货架上两年的价签。

examples.en: The lake froze hard enough to skate on.
examples.cn: 湖面冻得可以滑冰了。

examples.en: She froze when the teacher asked her a surprise question.
examples.cn: 老师突然提问时她一下子呆住了。

examples.en: Frozen peas taste almost as fresh as garden peas.
examples.cn: 冷冻豌豆尝起来几乎和新鲜的差不多。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「福瑞兹」——福气瑞气都冻住了，一动不动：freeze 就是万物被按下的暂停键。

root: freeze 出自日耳曼重构词根 *freusan（被寒冷灼伤），与 frost 同源；古英语 freosan 意为「凝固成冰」。强变化动词（freeze-froze-frozen）。核心意象是「流动停止」：水冻、人僵、价冻结共用一根。

sensesIntro.en: Freeze stops moving water, food time, startled bodies, and changing prices.
sensesIntro.cn: freeze 让流动的水、食物的时间、受惊的身体、变动的价格一并停住。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flowing thing suddenly held still
core.cn: 核心意象：流动之物骤然定住

branches.en: Liquids harden into ice
branches.cn: 液体变硬成冰

branches.en: Food time suspended in the freezer
branches.cn: 食物时间在冰柜中被暂停

branches.en: A startled body goes still
branches.cn: 受惊的身体僵住不动

branches.en: Prices and wages held in place
branches.cn: 价格与工资被钉在原地

branches.en: Stopping flow keeps things from spoiling
branches.cn: 止住流动使事物免于变坏

intro.en: Freeze heads a Germanic cold family rather than a Latin one.
intro.cn: freeze 统领的是日耳曼「寒冷家族」，而非拉丁词族。

latinIntro.en: The root *freusan links freeze and frost; Latin cooling words are separate borrowings.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 *freusan 连接 freeze 与 frost；拉丁冷却词是独立的借入成分。

items.example: Put the meat in the freezer.
A frigid wind blew all day.

definition_zh: 教堂；教会；礼拜；教会组织
definition_en: a building where Christians worship; the organized Christian religion; a church service
core_image: 尖顶房子里的钟声与长椅
scene: 周日清晨，小镇的钟声从老街尽头传来。 The family walks to the church every Sunday.

intro.en: Church goes back to a Greek word for the Lord's house, arriving via Germanic languages.
intro.cn: church 可追溯到希腊语「主的房子」，经日耳曼诸语传入英语。

items.en: Greek kyriakon meant the Lord's house or the Lord's thing.
items.cn: 希腊语 kyriakon 义为「主的房子」或「属于主的」。

items.en: Germanic languages borrowed it as kirika, seen in German Kirche.
items.cn: 日耳曼诸语借入为 kirika，见于德语 Kirche。

items.en: Old English cirice and circe carried the word into England.
items.cn: 古英语 cirice、circe 把这个词带入英格兰。

items.en: Old Norse kirkja influenced northern English forms like kirk.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 kirkja 影响了英格兰北部的 kirk 等形式。

items.en: Middle English spelling settled toward chirche and finally church.
items.cn: 中古英语拼写逐步定型为 chirche，最终是 church。

note.en: The first group gathers look-alikes; the second gathers worship words.
note.cn: 第一组收形近词，第二组收礼拜类词。

definition_en: to give time or money, to save, to forgive, or kept as extra
core_image: 柜子里放着一把备用钥匙，静静等着需要它的那天

senses.title: To give time or resources
senses.definition: to be able to give time, money, or effort to someone

definition_en: to be in a flat resting position; to be situated; to say something untrue; an untrue statement
core_image: 身体放平，静卧不动；或嘴一张，假话滑出
scene: 午后阳台，猫在毯子上翻了个身。 The old town lies beside a quiet river.
sceneCN: 这里 lie 是「位于」（第 2 个义项：坐落、位于）；句意为古城坐落在一条安静的河边。

derivatives.zh: lie 加指人后缀 -ar，指「说谎的人」
lie 加 -ing，指「说谎的；躺卧的」

senses.title: To be in a flat resting position
senses.definition: to put your body flat on a surface to rest
senses.definitionCN: 把身体平放在一个面上休息
senses.example: The cat lies on the warm mat all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 猫整个下午都躺在暖垫上。
senses.why: A body laid out flat is the plain physical picture.
senses.whyCN: 平放的身体是最直白的画面。

senses.title: To be situated
senses.definition: to be in a particular place or position
senses.definitionCN: 处于某地或某位置
senses.example: The old town lies beside a quiet river.
senses.exampleCN: 古城坐落在安静的河边。
senses.why: A place 'rests' where it is, so the body word extends to geography.
senses.whyCN: 地方「安卧」于其所在，身体之词便延伸到地理。

senses.title: To stay or remain in a state
senses.definition: to remain in a specified condition
senses.definitionCN: 保持于特定状态
senses.example: The papers lay untouched for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 文件一周没人碰。
senses.why: What lies somewhere also lies in some state; position and condition share the verb.
senses.whyCN: 躺于某处也即处于某状态，位置与状态共用此动词。

senses.title: To say something untrue
senses.definition: to make a false statement on purpose
senses.definitionCN: 故意作虚假陈述
senses.example: He lied about his age to join.
senses.exampleCN: 他谎报年龄报名。
senses.why: The mouth builds a false picture; a different verb grew beside the lying-down one.
senses.whyCN: 嘴构建假象；这个词与「躺卧」的词是并肩长成的另一个词。

senses.title: An untrue statement
senses.definition: something said that is known to be false
senses.definitionCN: 明知不实而言之事
senses.example: That story is a bare-faced lie.
senses.exampleCN: 那个说法是彻头彻尾的谎言。
senses.why: The false statement freezes into a noun anyone can point at.
senses.whyCN: 假陈述凝固成名词，人人可以指认。

senses.title: To be about to happen (lie ahead)
senses.definition: to be waiting in the future
senses.definitionCN: 在将来等待
senses.example: Greater tests lie ahead of us.
senses.exampleCN: 更大的考验在前方等着我们。
senses.why: The future stretches out before you like a road you have not walked.
senses.whyCN: 未来像未走的路在你面前铺开。

senses.title: To be buried or at rest (lie)
senses.definition: to be buried in a grave or resting place
senses.definitionCN: 安葬于墓穴或安息之所
senses.example: Her ashes lie beneath the old oak.
senses.exampleCN: 她的骨灰安放在老橡树下。
senses.why: Final rest is the last lying down, the verb\u0027s quietest use.
senses.whyCN: 最终安息是最后一次躺下，动词最安静的用法。

intro.en: Two verbs share the spelling lie. The posture word comes from Old English licgan, from Germanic ligan 'to lie down'; the falsehood word comes from Old English leogan 'to tell lies', from a root meaning 'to lie, be false'.
intro.cn: 两个动词共用拼写 lie。姿态词来自古英语 licgan，出自日耳曼语 ligan「躺下」；谎言词来自古英语 leogan「说谎」，词根意为「不实」。

items.en: Old English licgan meant 'to lie, be situated', the posture verb used across English ever since.
items.cn: 古英语 licgan 意为「躺、位于」，姿态动词沿用至今。

items.en: Germanic ligan is behind the posture verb, kin to German liegen and Dutch liggen.
items.cn: 日耳曼语 ligan 是姿态动词的来源，与德语 liegen、荷兰语 liggen 同族。

items.en: Old English leogan meant 'to tell falsehoods', a separate verb with its own root.
items.cn: 古英语 leogan 意为「说谎」，是与姿态词无关的独立动词。

items.en: The falsehood root spread through Germanic, giving German lugen 'to peer, spy' in some dialects.
items.cn: 谎言词根遍布日耳曼语族，某些方言给出德语 lugen「窥视」。

items.en: In Middle English the two verbs kept distinct past forms while sharing one spelling.
items.cn: 中古英语里两动词过去式分立，仅共享一个拼写。

note.en: Group one flags the famous confusions; group two lists rest and falsehood words.
note.cn: 第一组标出著名易混词；第二组列出休憩与谎言词。
